endorsements.quote: When faced with a clinical problem that is overly complex, ML teams should consider focusing on a different, less complex problem that is well-encoded in the training data and whose success can be easily measured in a time horizon that is clinically meaningful.
First, can we define a single decision and its success metric in ≤1 sentence?

Problem selection is a challenging exercise requiring engagement of the entire multidisciplinary ML team, but there lacks a practical framework to guide discussions in a way that leads to meaningful candidate problem evaluation.
First, is there a definable action that can be taken within the clinically appropriate time frame after the model’s prediction that is plausibly linked to an improved outcome?
Though the elements of the checklist have empirical basis, multidisciplinary discussion is required to decide whether to pursue the candidate problem through the lens of actionability.

unlisted_practices: ML teams should evaluate candidate clinical problems for optimal complexity, neither too complex nor too simple, before building clinical decision support.
ML teams should assess whether decision support alerts would prompt actions that would not otherwise occur based on the care team's interpretation of readily available data alone.
ML teams should estimate the expected rate of non-actionable alerts and confirm it is below care team and unit tolerance.
Teams should use a complexity-actionability problem evaluation checklist in which every item must receive a yes for a candidate problem to pass.
Teams should gather empirical evidence, such as case vignettes or simulation scenarios, when consensus on problem selection cannot be reached.
Teams should publish their problem evaluation checklist methods and results as supplemental material accompanying clinical decision support reports.
Health systems should pair clinical decision support with clinical execution support using closed-loop control under clinician supervision to standardize treatment execution.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/framework paper proposing the CAPE checklist for clinical problem selection in ML-based decision support, providing guidance on how healthcare organizations and ML teams should select and govern AI deployment targets.
